solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tiny little daughter fighting shark?

parts.note: D is the short form of daughter, as in family trees
fighting is war
a shark is an example of a fish, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A small girl squares up to a shark in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfish describes something unusually small in stature, a synonym for tiny.

clue.text: Bill in old accommodation set up again from the start

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the whole is read from the bottom upwards
in means the bill letters go inside the accommodation word

parts.note: a pad is slang for a place to live
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A bill for an old lodging gets drawn up all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces give OPACAD, which reads upwards as the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Da capo is the musical instruction to go back and repeat from the beginning.

clue.text: Gangster gets money as early as this

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster
the ready is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A mobster is paid off so soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' or 'readies' is British slang for available cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, earlier than expected, the sense of so soon.

clue.text: Broken-up female thinking about practical joke

parts.note: a rag is a student prank
mental means relating to thinking

explanation.surface: A woman broken by a cruel prank keeps thinking about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag in British student slang is a prank or the charity stunts of rag week.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragmental means made of fragments, in pieces, hence broken up.

clue.text: Awfully shy PE teacher keeping quiet — encouragement needed to talk

indicators.note: keeping means the jumbled letters hold the quiet letter inside
awfully suggests these words are badly messed up, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A painfully shy gym teacher, tongue-tied, needs encouragement to speak up.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech therapy helps people with stammers or impairments learn to speak, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Mount near Jerusalem to be found in Old Testament

indicators.note: found in says the word for 'to be' sits inside the Testament letters

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A traveller's note that a certain mountain near Jerusalem is mentioned in the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mount of Olives is also called Olivet.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivet is the older name for the Mount of Olives, the hill east of Jerusalem's old city.

clue.text: Parrot shows resplendence with head concealed

indicators.note: with head concealed says the first letter is hidden away, dropped

parts.note: glory is splendour, resplendence

explanation.surface: A parrot shows off its splendid plumage while tucking its head away.
explanation.definitionFit: A lory is a brightly coloured small parrot of Australasia, related to lorikeets.

clue.text: Physicist inventing tube is daring — no good missing out

indicators.note: missing out means those letters are left out of the word

parts.note: venturing means daring, taking a risk

explanation.surface: A physicist's tube invention is bold, though nothing good came of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Venturi was the Italian scientist after whom the Venturi tube, a constricted pipe, is named.

clue.text: Group of soldiers in army secures agreements

indicators.note: in means the soldiers go inside the army letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
to secure is to tie, so ties

explanation.surface: A unit stationed within an army is bound by treaties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers and the Territorial Army are British Army staples of crosswords; 'secures' is a verb meaning fastens.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal agreements made between nations or states.

clue.text: Bob not half a scoundrel

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word for bob is kept, here its front three letters

parts.note: to bob is to make a quick curtsy

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about a fellow called Bob being only partly a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the little dip a curtsy makes. Half of CURTSY is CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a contemptible man, literally a mongrel dog, so a scoundrel.

clue.text: Destroyer of trees and fruit initiated by a man

indicators.note: initiated by means the fruit word is started off by what follows, so those pieces come first

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
an orange is a fruit

explanation.surface: A man introduces something that destroys trees and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer of trees and fruit' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'trees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was the defoliant herbicide sprayed over forests in the Vietnam War, stripping trees bare.

clue.text: Vulgarity that may render everything bland

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lack of good taste, crudeness
second meaning, read literally: having no flavour at all, which makes all food bland

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word literally, as having no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both a lack of aesthetic judgment and literally lacking any flavour.

clue.text: Drug supplier peaceful type? Not if embracing hurt

indicators.note: embracing means the shortened word holds the hurt word inside it
Not if says the two letters of if are to be left out of the peaceful type

parts.note: a pacifist is a person committed to peace
taken as written
to hurt is to harm

explanation.surface: A dealer muses that a peaceful person is not one who embraces causing hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Not if' read like a debate about pacifism; 'Not' is an instruction to strike out the two letters of 'if'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines, so is a supplier of drugs in the medical sense.

clue.text: Dublin money once used for gamble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Irish pound, the currency before the euro
second meaning: a bet, especially a speculative one

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings are the same four letters: the old Irish currency and a slang word for a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: The punt was Ireland's pound until 2002, and to take a punt is British slang for a wager.

clue.text: Container with a lentil mistaken for another plant

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters of a lentil are got wrong, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pot holding a lentil gets taken for some other plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to the lentil, itself a plant; LENTIL rearranged gives ENTILL, and A ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Potentilla, the cinquefoil, is a flowering garden shrub of the rose family.

clue.text: Young bird caught by good trap — finally flying into it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: finally, in the editor's corrected clue, picks the last letter of by

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A young bird is captured in a net, having flown straight into it.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue has a slip: the last letter of 'flying' is G, not Y. The Times editor apologised and corrected it to 'Young bird caught finally by good trap', where 'finally' takes Y from the end of 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a baby swan, so a young bird of a particular kind.

clue.text: Poem about child who lived in biblical nation?

indicators.note: about means the poem word is turned round

parts.note: an ode is a poem
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A poem about a child who lived in a nation from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the person rather than a noun, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An Edomite was an inhabitant of Edom, the kingdom south of the Dead Sea in the Old Testament.

clue.text: The pools could disguise these awful pits

indicators.note: could disguise means the letters can be dressed up in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Puddles on the road may hide nasty holes beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Puddles hiding potholes are a familiar road hazard, so the surface fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Potholes are holes in a road surface, the sort of pits a driver dreads.

clue.text: Hoarding silver is bizarre? It's a scandal

indicators.note: hoarding means the word for bizarre keeps the silver symbol stashed inside

parts.note: outré means unconventional, bizarre
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether stockpiling silver is weird, and declares it scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTRE is a French borrowing meaning beyond the bounds of the usual.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is an act or event causing public shock, much as a scandal does.

clue.text: Endlessly irritable educationist means to create experimental environment

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: testy means irritable
BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree

explanation.surface: A tetchy teacher tries to create a setting for experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A test bed is a facility or setup for trying out new machinery or ideas.

clue.text: Issue of this writer securing little work after office's closure

indicators.note: after puts what follows behind that letter
closure means the word's ending, its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of office

indicators.note: securing means me holds the unit of work inside it

parts.note: this writer means the setter, me
an erg is a tiny physics unit of work

explanation.surface: A writer reports producing a little work after the office has shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to come out; an erg is a tiny physics unit, hence 'little work'.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out, and to emerge is to come out into view, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Golf and aquatic sport becoming more popular?

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rowing is a water sport

explanation.surface: A question whether golf and rowing are catching on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something growing is increasing, as in a growing following or rising popularity.

clue.text: Trendy girl coming out, student ultimately needing a loan?

parts.note: in means fashionable
a deb, debutante, is a girl entering society

indicators.note: ultimately means take only the last letter of student

explanation.surface: A fashionable debutante and a student, both short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming out here is the society debut of a debutante.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in debt means owing money, often the state of someone who needs to borrow.

clue.text: Quiet hours allowing you and me to tuck in

indicators.note: to tuck in means the pair go inside the hours letters

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for hour, doubled for the plural
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Quiet hours in which the two of us can tuck into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in' sounds like eating; here it means go inside, between the two H's.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush is silence or stillness, used as a noun meaning quiet.

clue.text: Old instrument given new life — something worth having husband collected

indicators.note: collected means the word for given new life gathers the other pieces inside

parts.note: someone born has been given new life
an asset is something valuable to have

explanation.surface: An old instrument restored, valued enough for a husband to collect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given new life' reads as restoration of the instrument, but it simply means born, which wraps round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is a tenor clarinet of the 18th century, an instrument Mozart wrote for.

clue.text: Monarch at home in poetic isle

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
in means at home

explanation.surface: A king or queen at home on an island in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland.

clue.text: One of the aspirations of the French inventor to make national symbol

parts.words: One of the aspirations of the French
parts.note: liberty is one of the three ideals in France's motto, liberty, equality, fraternity
Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary ideal joins an inventor to make a symbol of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' looks like a demand for a French word, but it is the French motto being cited in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberty Bell in Philadelphia is an emblem of American independence.

clue.text: Something maybe in freezer that is keeping cold

indicators.note: keeping means those letters hold the cold letter inside

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Something in the freezer is what keeps food cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cubes and frozen water are typical contents of a freezer, so this is an example.

clue.text: Track has one slipping, left abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means the left letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: slipping is sliding

explanation.surface: A rough track has someone slipping and leaving it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short railway track off the main line where trains are parked.

clue.text: Food in shell is French, load being imported

indicators.note: being imported means the load is brought inside the French word

parts.note: est is French for is
cargo is a load carried by a ship

explanation.surface: A shellfish dish turns out to be French, its load being imported.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French culinary snail, eaten served in its own shell.
